newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PSE builds on Tuesday gains, up 0.85 pct.
newsitem.headline: Czech PSE builds on Tuesday gains, up 0.85 pct.

text.p: The Prague Stock Exchange, for the first time in nearly one month, recorded its first back- to-back advancing session on Wednesday, though dealers said they saw little reason for change in the bourse's fortunes.
Komercni Banka, SPT Telecom, CEZ, Chemopetrol, Investicni Banka all closed higher to boost the PX50 index 4.2 points, or 0.85 percent, to 499.8.
The PX50 gained 1.35 percent on Tuesday and despite posting its first two-session advance since June 11-12, dealers remain muted on the propects of a sustained uptrend on the bourse.
"You have gains to a few major shares pulling the rest of the market higher, but there really aren't any signs of a change in the bearish sentiment right now," said one local trader.
The Czech market has been on a gradual decline for most of the year, hit hard by investor complaints of murky trading practices and a lack of timely company information.
On the broader market, most shares made little major moves, with the exception of ceramics maker ZC Kaolinove Zavody which fell 125 crowns to 2,393.
Overall trading was average with 575,183 shares changing hands on turnover of 679.1 million crowns. Some 113 issues closed higher on the session, while 112 fell and 44 were unchanged.

Dealers noted that a cloud loomed over the market for most of the day after it was revealed that U.S.-born Michael Hobbs, founding partner of the Czech brokerage firm Atlantik Financni Trhy and one of the pioneers of the post-Communist market.

Hobbs, 37, who was working closely with the Prague Stock Exchange on the creation of a Securities Exchange Commission, was found by colleagues in the bathtub of his company-owned flat last Thursday and had been dead for about one week.

The market was filled with rumours about Hobbs's death, but police said that there were no signs of violence. An official cause of death had not been determined because medical examiners cannot perform an autopsy until relatives arrive from the United States.

"(Foul play) was ruled out but the cause of death -- whether it was heart failure or anything else... (the doctors) did not dare to estimate, because of the condition of the body, until after the autopsy," a police spokesman said.
Hobbs, a native of San Diego, came to the former Czechoslovakia in 1991 to teach finance at Masaryk University in the Czech second city of Brno.

There he co-founded Atlantik in 1993 along with his former students Daniel Gladis and Karel Bastl, setting up a thriving business alongside the country's massive post-Communist privatisation programme.

Last summer, Hobbs resigned his executive position in the company after he said his partners had called an extraordinary shareholders meeting of the limited liability company to strip him of his authority.
